title: Failover telemetry gaps — postmortem and playbook updates
content:
Summary:

During a planned west-us -> eu-west traffic shift test on 2025-02-18 we observed a longer-than-expected tail of elevated 5xxs and increased client latency after DNS weight changes. The operator steps completed the DNS and routing changes on schedule, but the customer-facing error rate persisted for ~18 minutes before gradual recovery. This exercise surfaced multiple telemetry blindspots that delayed confident decision-making and led to a conservative rollback.

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes of degraded success rate post-shift (start 2025-02-18T15:12 UTC, recovery ~15:30 UTC)
- Affected scope: subset of API routes (chat-generation, streaming responses) hitting eu-west backend with warmed routing but cold KV cache state for some customers
- Visible symptoms: increased 5xx rate (502/504), client streaming stalls, burst of retry traffic from SDKs

Detection timeline (high-level):
- 15:10 UTC: operator flips weighted DNS in console (target eu-west weight 60%)
- 15:12 UTC: control-plane confirms DNS update; global LB starts shifting traffic
- 15:14 UTC: dashboards show spike in 5xxs from eu-west; SLO alert thresholds not hit due to aggregated metric smoothing
- 15:18 UTC: on-call triggered to check routing; KV cache miss rate not visible per-region in dashboards, operator proceeds with standard warm-standby checklist
- 15:26 UTC: manual query dig shows some edge nodes still resolving to west-us (TTL/prop variation); operator begins rollback to prevent customer impact
- 15:30 UTC: gradual recovery observed; TTL propagation and backend cache warmup cited in postmortem

Root cause analysis (summary):
1) KV cache warmup visibility gap: we have only cluster/global kvcache hit/miss metrics on dashboards. During region shifts we need per-region kvcache_preseed_hit_rate and outstanding preseed queue length to know whether the target region already holds warmed prefixes for common requests. No alert existed for low preseed hit-rate during failover.

2) DNS propagation variance: some of the CDN/edge nodes cached the old mapping longer than expected (unexpected TTL retention on legacy edge layer). We had a mild mismatch between our planned DNS TTLs and the CDN caching behavior. There was no telemetry that measured the per-POP DNS resolution distribution during a weight shift.

3) Aggregated SLO smoothing: our primary SLO alert aggregates across regions with a 5-min rolling window, masking short high-impact spikes during transition. The lack of a short-window regional SLO caused slower on-call detection.

4) Runbook friction: the operator checklist assumed kvcache would warm quickly; there was no mandatory verification step (a quick kvcache probe) before declaring the shift complete.

Telemetry gaps discovered:
- Missing per-region kvcache_preseed_hit_rate metric. We only collect at host/cluster granularity.
- No per-region DNS resolution histogram (which POPs are resolving to which origin during a rollout).
- Lack of synthetic failover smoke test (pre-shift) that validates both DNS resolution and kvcache preseed for a sample customer set.
- No short-window (30s–1m) regional SLO alerting for critical routes.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Rolled back DNS weights to previous steady-state at 15:26 UTC to stop error amplification (operator decision logged).
- Increased alerting sensitivity for aggregate 1m error rate while participating teams investigated (temporary measure).
- Operators ran targeted kvcache preseed for top 20 customer prefixes into eu-west (manual job) to accelerate warmup.

Post-incident actions (short-term, to complete within 2 weeks):
- SRE-476: Add per-region kvcache_preseed_hit_rate metric and dashboard (owner: Arjun).
  - Instrumentation: export region tag with kvcache metrics from preseed workers.
  - Dashboard: show 1m/5m trend for preseed hit rate + outstanding queue length.

- INF-1234: Create per-POP DNS resolution telemetry (owner: Sofia).
  - Small agent on edge nodes to emit resolution target histogram every 10s.
  - Alert rule if >2% of POPs still resolving to source region after configured safety window.

- Short-window SLOs: update critical-route SLOs to include a 1-minute regional alert (owner: Priya).

- Runbook update: add mandatory kvcache verification step in the traffic-shift checklist (owner: Liam).
  - New step: run kvcache_probe --region eu-west --prefixes top-20 and require preseed_hit_rate >= 90% before finalizing shift.
  - If preseed_hit_rate < 90% then hold shift and (a) trigger immediate preseed job and (b) re-evaluate after 2 minutes.

Longer-term improvements (Q2 roadmap):
- Synthetic pre-shift smoke harness: create a synthetic runner that can simulate a sample cross-region client and validate DNS+LB mapping + kvcache presence end-to-end (linked INF epic).
- Edge CDN contract: review caching/TTL behavior with CDN provider and align TTL semantics to avoid hidden retention.
- Failover rehearsal cadence: add quarterly full failover rehearsals that include synthetic client verification and operator time-to-decision metrics.
- Graceful degrade policy: implement automatic partial-traffic fallback to model-variant with lower state dependency for the first 3 minutes of a region shift.

Runbook (proposed new play sequence for region weight shift):
1) Pre-shift checks (operator):
   - Confirm target region health (healthcheck: curl -sSf https://eu-west-edge/health)
   - Verify recent deploys: no model/serving changes in last 24h
   - Run kvcache_probe --region <target> --prefixes top-N -> require preseed_hit_rate >= 90%
   - Run dns-smoke --from=3-pop-edges --target=<region> and confirm >95% resolve to target weight within safety window

2) Flip weight to 10% (canary) -> monitor 30s windows for 1m SLOs and kvcache metrics

3) If any 1m regional SLO > threshold OR preseed_hit_rate < 80%: immediately revert and run manual preseed job

4) Progressive ramp (10% -> 30% -> 60%) with 2-minute observation at each step and run preseed_probe as needed

5) Finalize shift only after 10 minutes of stable 1m SLOs and kvcache_preseed_hit_rate >= 95%

Example operator commands and checks (for playbook):
- kvcache_probe usage:
  - ./kvcache_probe --region eu-west --prefixes-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt --timeout 60s --output json
  - check JSON field preseed_hit_rate and outstanding_queue_length
- DNS check (from an edge node):
  - dig +short @<local-resolver> api.redwood.example.com | sort | uniq -c
  - dns-smoke --target eu-west --sample 50 --duration 30s
- Quick health endpoints:
  - curl -sSf https://eu-west-edge/api/v1/health | jq .status

Out-of-band notes for infra/APIs teams:
- kvcache_probe needs a small API change to return per-prefix status and region tag (PR: infra#987).
- Router control-plane should emit an event when weight flips include a "planned-shift-id" to correlate across DNS, LB, and preseed systems.

Retrospective observations and non-actionable learnings:
- Cold cache effects are highly non-linear for streaming routes; a small fraction of cold prefixes drove disproportionate streaming stalls. We should prioritize preseed for prefixes that map to streaming sessions.
- Operators currently rely heavily on intuition from past rehearsals; formalizing decision thresholds reduced time-to-decision in the rollback.

Open questions for follow-ups:
- What is an acceptable safety window for DNS TTLs given CDN behavior? (action: engage CDN partner)
- Should we automate preseed triggers as part of weight flip orchestration? (tradeoff: increased background work during false positives)

Action owner summary (short):
- Arjun Patel: instrument per-region kvcache metrics (SRE-476)
- Sofia Alvarez: per-POP DNS telemetry agent + dashboard (INF-1234)
- Priya Rao: short-window SLO alert updates
- Liam O'Neill: runbook change + operator training module
- Maya Chen: coordinate failover rehearsal schedule and write synthetic smoke runner spec

Appendix: quick reproducer notes:
- Reproduce locally with dev-edge overlay: run local dns-smoke with weight flips between 127.0.0.1:8080 and 127.0.0.2:8080 while toggling preseed workers to simulate cold/warm states.
- Attach logs: look for kvcache preseed worker traces (preseed.start/complete), router weight-change event IDs, and edge resolver cache TTL logs.

If anything is unclear or you want a condensed one-pager for on-call, ping #sre-playbooks and reference this doc.
